summary:
Heimdall is a web dashboard that organizes 23 combustion-science
 investigations from NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database —
 including BASS, Saffire I–III, FLEX, ACME, SPICE, and SLICE — and makes
 them searchable, comparable, and rankable for spacecraft fire-safety
 work.

 A transparent scoring engine ranks studies against five mission
 scenarios (Earth, ISS, lunar base/rover, Mars base, spacesuit) across
 four weighted factors — atmosphere match, gravity regime, data coverage,
 and documentation — each with a visible score breakdown. A function-
 calling AI copilot answers questions by executing real dataset queries
 (search, detail, ranking, prediction) and streams its tool calls live.
 FireHazR, a pre-trained KNN model on FLEX droplet trials, predicts
 microgravity burn duration for methanol and heptane, and abstains
 outside its coverage envelope. Users compare studies side by side,
 export CSV matrices, and navigate an illustrative 3D mission hub.

 Heimdall never fabricates values: PSI measurements are ingested as
 recorded, and lunar-gravity results are presented as bounds, not
 predictions.
details:
Heimdall ingests NASA Physical Science Informatics (PSI) experimental-

table exports for 23 combustion investigations — BASS, BASS-II, Saffire

I–III, FLEX/FLEX-2, CFI/CFI-G, the six ACME studies, SPICE, SLICE,

SoFIE, SAME/SAME-R, DAFT/DAFT-2 — plus two upcoming studies (LUCI, FM2)

shown as placeholders. Per-run measurements are merged into measured

condition ranges (O₂ min/max, pressure, flow velocity) that are

physically bounded and never extrapolated; unparseable values are

dropped, not guessed. Everything is stored in MongoDB and served through

a Node/Express API to a React dashboard.

On top of that data layer sit four capabilities: a catalog with per-

study detail and telemetry pages; a ranking engine that scores studies

against five mission scenarios (Earth, ISS, lunar base/rover, Mars base,

spacesuit) using four weighted factors — atmosphere match, gravity

regime, data coverage, documentation — and returns the full per-factor

breakdown; a side-by-side comparator with a differences-only view, an

O₂–pressure regime map, and CSV export; and FireHazR, a pre-trained KNN

model on FLEX droplet trials that predicts microgravity burn duration

for methanol and heptane only, returning real neighbors and weights —

and abstaining with a reason outside its coverage envelope. An agentic

AI copilot answers questions by executing real tools (dataset search,

study detail, ranking, burn-duration prediction, scenario listing),

streaming each tool call and token live over SSE, with automatic

failover across Gemini, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and the Devin

API.

Benefits and intended impact

It turns decades of scattered PSI results into something findable,

comparable, and honestly ranked — aimed at engineers sizing atmospheres

for future lunar/Martian habitats (≥30% O₂ at reduced pressure), and at

students and researchers who need to locate relevant experiments fast.

Transparency is the point: every score shows its factors, every

prediction shows its neighbors, and every AI answer traces to executed

dataset queries.

Tools and software

React 19 + Vite + Three.js (React Three Fiber) + Recharts frontend; Node

+ Express 5 + Mongoose API; Python FastAPI analytics service; MongoDB

(Atlas or local Docker); Blender for low-poly glTF planet models; Web

Audio API for synthesized sound. The copilot runs through Gemini,

OpenAI-compatible, or Devin API providers.

Creativity

Honesty is engineered in: the model abstains rather than estimates,

0g/1g results are presented as bounds because PSI has no partial-gravity

data, and the 3D planet viewer is deliberately decoupled from the

predictor so selecting Mars never injects invented conditions.

Factors considered

Scientific accuracy over visual flash, degraded-state behavior (if

analytics is down the UI says so instead of fabricating), provider

failover for the demo, and accessibility (reduced motion, keyboard

navigation).
dataRefs: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
